author: cli
text: THE QUEUE DOES NOT APPLY THE RING RULE, so it over-reports by an order of magnitude. stale_notes at query.py:1017 counts every entry carrying en['stale'], never routing through for_display()/unsuperseded_stale(). Measured on this repo 2026-08-16: attention says 'stale knowledge entries: 43'; the decisive queue is 3. The other 40 are superseded history - somebody already answered them, and the answer is sitting directly above in the same channel. The number 43 is exactly the count of entries that have a newer entry behind them, which is the tell. This is the 0.54.2 lesson ('superseded is not stale - the first is a warning, the second is history, and a surface that renders them identically teaches people to ignore both') reappearing in the one surface literally named 'the queue', and it is CLAUDE.md lesson 7's failure mode: unsuperseded_stale is supposed to be THE one ring rule, and verify_change asks it correctly at query.py:70-71 while this counts by hand. Direction is safe - it raises warnings nobody needs, never suppresses one they did - but a queue that reads 43 when 3 are actionable is a queue nobody works. Related: summary reports superseded: 0 on the same data, which should be 43. FIX: route through for_display + unsuperseded_stale, and pin it with a fixture where a superseded stale entry must NOT be counted.

author: cli
text: CORRECTION, supersedes the note below it: the attention half stands, the summary half was wrong. attention DOES over-report (43 raw vs 3 decisive on this repo 2026-08-16; ambient knowledge_lag, reading the same data, correctly says 3) and stale_notes at query.py:1017 does count by hand without the ring rule. But 'summary reports superseded: 0 which should be 43' is FALSE. summary.knowledge.superseded counts COORDINATES RETIRED BY A RENAME whose knowledge migrated to a successor - a lineage concept computed at query.py:399-427 and pinned by tests/test_mcp.py:304 (assert == 1 after exactly one rename). Measured here: 234 lineage old-refs, 0 retired coordinates still holding knowledge, so 0 is the TRUE value. for_display()['superseded'] at metadata.py:133 is a different concept entirely - an ENTRY with a newer entry in its channel. THE REAL DEFECT IS THE NAME: one word, 'superseded', names two unrelated things on two surfaces, and reading both carefully I still conflated them and filed a false defect against correct code. A number that is right can still mislead if its name is claimed by something else. Whoever unifies these surfaces must NOT make them agree - they are answering different questions and should be named so they cannot be read as one.

author: cli
text: FIXED in 0.55.2 - supersedes the correction below, which supersedes the original report. The hand count at query.py:1017 is gone: attention now asks for_display + unsuperseded_stale, the same rule ambient _knowledge_lag has always asked. Measured on this repo across the change: 43 -> 3, with ambient agreeing at 3 both before and after. The correction's warning was heeded - summary.knowledge.superseded was NOT touched, because it counts retired coordinates and 0 is its true value here. Three tests now hold this: a fixture carrying both a superseded stale entry and a live one (a fixture with only live entries passes against the hand count, which is the version that would have proved nothing), a surfaces-agree test, and a structural pin in tests/test_read_fence.py extending the stamp_for no-reimplementation guard to unsuperseded_stale and for_display. All three were falsified by restoring the hand count and all three failed.

author: cli
text: ATTENTION TRUNCATES COMMENT ROT SILENTLY, and its own sibling in the same return dict does not. rot = rot[:limit] at query.py:982 with limit=20, and the payload carries NO comment_rot_total - while markers, three lines away, ships marker_total alongside the truncated list. So a reader sees 20 and cannot tell whether that is all of them or the first 20 of any number. Measured on this repo 2026-08-16 under 0.55.3: the TRUE total is 49; every report of 'comment rot: 20' this session, including mine to the user across several releases, was a truncated list read as a census. An independent reviewer evaluating the MCP tools the same day reported 'found 10 functions with comment rot' - a different truncation, same false impression, from a person who had no way to know either. This is the no-silent-caps rule that the rest of the codebase already keeps: downstream reports is_lower_bound, dig labels a shallow clone as a lower bound, get_parsers records and surfaces every skipped language rather than dropping it quietly. One surface in this very function obeys it and its neighbour does not, which is the same second-copy shape as the ring rule this function was fixed for in 0.55.2. FIX: report comment_rot_total (and stale_design_docs total) exactly as marker_total already is, and say 'showing N of M' in the CLI printer.
